paragraphs: Every branch pane now compresses like Chess Tempo. A move with exactly one reply keeps flowing on the same horizontal line (1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.e5 c5, one continuous chain); only a real fork — two or more replies — drops to an indented branch list, and each branch is compressed the same way from there. This replaced the old one-move-per-row vertical list in all three branch panes (the admin Opening Tree Editor, the read-only course-chapter view, and My Repertoire) through one shared renderer (chainTreeHTML/chainNodeHTML), so the layout, the board-sync-on-click and the right-click menu all…

The blunder interrogation (Trim) already did most of what a "hardcoded MSPC wizard" would, chronologically, per mistake, before this session: M/S/P as Socratic questions judged locally for free (Stockfish and the position's own facts, no API call) with an AI double-check only when a member's tier allows it, C as playing the better move on the board with Stockfish judging it live (with the brilliant / great move celebrations already built in), and a verdict that updates the player's profile struggles — scoped strictly to that mistake's facts, never the whole game, so it can't fixate on an…

requirements.text: CONFIG.ladder.access sets the membership each paid level needs (default: vault, the Accelerator).
Masters currently needs the Accelerator like the other paid levels; a mentorship-only level needs one more lock level in the hub.
The public Lichess endpoint takes a difficulty level, not a rating: without a Lichess login its levels sit around 900, 1200, 1500, 1800 and 2100.
Below 900 Lichess can't match a rating without a login, which is what the bank is for.
